title: The Prayer of Manasseh
lead: A fifteen-verse Greek prayer of repentance in the name of King Manasseh of Judah, written to give the words of the prayer that 2 Chronicles 33:18–19 says he prayed in captivity. Orthodox churches read it at Great Compline, mostly in Lent; most Western churches keep it among the Apocrypha or leave it out.

sections.b: The prayer is not in the Hebrew Bible. It survives in Christian church orders (the Didascalia Apostolorum and the Apostolic Constitutions, book 2, section 22), among the odes copied after the Psalms in Greek manuscripts such as Codex Alexandrinus, and in Latin manuscripts and printed Bibles, where the Clementine Vulgate set it in an appendix. Readers of English met it as "The Prayer of Manasses" in the Apocrypha of the KJV.
